default.p.test-1-p1.vietnamese:
Regarding note-taking, I would like to mention a few points to keep in mind first.

The first is that I hope you will not be distracted by drawing perfectly straight lines or making beautifully neat marks.

I sometimes see people using colored ballpoint pens or highlighters to draw beautiful lines or take notes in books and materials, but these people often fail to absorb the content.

What matters most in the end is reading and understanding the text quickly and accurately. When taking notes, it is enough to draw freely by hand and do so quickly. Since it is sufficient to understand your notes when you read them again later, being more meticulous and neat than that is nothing more than a completely pointless waste of time.

（※1）Drawing freely by hand: writing or drawing without using tools such as a ruler.

default.p.test-10-p1.vietnamese:
Stretching once a day is enough. At first, do only as many repetitions as you can manage, then gradually increase the number.

Knee-Hug Exercise
～A stretch for the back and lower back～

First, lie on your back (※1), bring your legs together, and bend your knees. Hold your right knee with both hands, pull it close to your chest, and hold that position for 10 seconds. At this time, be careful not to leave a gap between your back and the floor. Do the same with the other leg, the left leg.

Next, hold both knees with both hands, pull them tightly toward your chest, and hold them there for 10 seconds. The key is to be aware that the muscles from your lower back to your buttocks are being stretched.

（※1）Lying on your back (aomuke): having your face and the front of your body facing upward.

default.p.test-12-p1.vietnamese:
When arranging a business appointment, people communicate the purpose by phone or email, then decide on a date, time, and duration that fit the other person's schedule. They also inform the other person of the number of visitors. It is more considerate to send an email before calling. Things will go more smoothly if you suggest several possible dates in advance. (The middle section has been omitted)

The same applies when visiting someone's private home: it is better to send an email before calling. This is because it gives the other person time to think instead of forcing them to answer immediately. If they do not want the visit, they can think of a reason to decline. If you do not know their email address, it is very polite to write in a letter or postcard: "I would like to ask permission to visit you regarding this matter. What is your schedule like? I will contact you again by phone at around ... o'clock."

（※1）Appointment: An arrangement or advance booking to meet someone or hold a meeting

（※2）Immediate answer: Answering a question right away

（※3）Excuse: A reason used to avoid answering directly or to justify or defend oneself

default.p.test-13-p1.vietnamese:
One of the most significant ways humans differ from other animals is their ability to use fire. Thanks to fire, humans were able to protect themselves from other animals and also remain active at night.

Humans are estimated to have acquired fire about one million years ago. The most significant effect that the use of fire may have had on the subsequent evolution of humanity was that it made cooking possible. At that time, the range of foods humans could eat was extremely limited, but by cooking or roasting things that could not be eaten raw, the range gradually increased.

① Eating cooked food brought changes to the human body. For example, gorillas mainly eat plants, but they must eat a large amount of vegetation each day to obtain enough nutrition. Since fresh plants are tough, their cheek muscles must be stronger in order to chew them. As a result, the skull (※1) surrounding the brain could not grow very large. Humans, on the other hand, began eating soft, cooked food, so their teeth and jaws became smaller, and the muscles used for chewing gradually weakened. In return, the skull is thought to have grown larger, and the vocal organs in the throat developed as well. In this way, humans developed bodies capable of possessing thought and language.

（※1）Skull: the bones of the head.

default.p.test-14-p1.outline.0.note: The author introduces having studied the tea ceremony for several years and describes the refreshing relaxation and moderate tension it provides.

default.p.test-14-p1.outline.2.note: The author shares a convenient office method for preparing matcha quickly, explains why they like it (convenience and no need to dispose of tea leaves), and asserts that the most important thing is that the tea tastes good. default.p.test-14-p1.vietnamese:
There are many disciplines whose names contain “the Way,” but the one I have been studying for the past few years is the tea ceremony. One enjoys and appreciates the slightly bitter green powder according to prescribed rules of procedure. A tea-ceremony practice session is a moment when time passes in a way completely different from casually drinking a cup of tea prepared at home. Its uniquely moderate tension, absent from everyday life, refreshes my mind.

My teacher might scold me for saying this, but the procedures themselves are genuinely troublesome. The appeal of the tea ceremony lies not only in the extraordinary atmosphere that fills the tearoom. The color, taste, and aroma of matcha are also among its attractions. Is there perhaps a way to enjoy this delicious pale green drink in a simpler, more relaxed manner? If I could drink a cup of matcha during a break at work, how relaxing that would be...

That is why I have recently been trying a small initiative. I keep all the tea-ceremony utensils ready in an office storage cabinet. I quickly prepare tea at work and share the appeal of that gentle green color with my colleagues. I used to keep ordinary tea leaves at work, but after realizing that matcha is convenient because there are no used leaves to dispose of, I became captivated by ① this method. Matcha is a beverage, after all, so enjoying it deliciously is naturally the most important thing, right?

(※1) Procedure: predetermined methods and rules for doing something

(※2) Making tea: preparing tea

(※3) Hamatte: being absorbed in something, enthusiastically devoted to it, and finding it perfectly suited to one's tastes

default.p.test-15-p1.outline.0.label: One-handed sign-language communication when the other hand is occupied
default.p.test-15-p1.outline.0.note: Introduces the phenomenon of people with hearing impairments communicating with only one hand when the other hand is occupied, such as when carrying something, riding a bicycle, or driving.
default.p.test-15-p1.outline.1.label: Redundancy in sign language and non-manual elements
default.p.test-15-p1.outline.1.note: The passage explains how redundancy—multiple layers of features—allows people to understand a message even when one arm's movement is missing, and discusses the roles of facial expressions, the eyes, and the mouth. Evidence for Question 1.
default.p.test-15-p1.outline.2.label: Communication entirely without using the hands, through facial expressions and eye contact
default.p.test-15-p1.outline.2.note: Gives practical examples of deaf people communicating without their hands or voices, using their eyes, chin, cheeks, lips, and mouth movements (basis for Question 2).
default.p.test-15-p1.outline.3.label: Vocabulary explanations and notes in the passage
default.p.test-15-p1.outline.3.note: Explanatory notes defining the asterisk-marked terms (※1 through ※4) in the text.
default.p.test-15-p1.vietnamese:
When one hand is occupied with carrying something, holding a bicycle’s handlebars, or holding an umbrella, a deaf person communicates using only the other hand. There are also cases in which a deaf person driving a car holds the steering wheel with one hand and communicates in sign language with the other. Incidentally, the responses of a deaf person sitting in the back seat can be seen in the rearview mirror.

In sign language, the features of words and sentences are incorporated in multiple layers, and one characteristic is that people can understand the whole message even when part of it is missing. This is called redundancy, and thanks to this characteristic, communication can still be understood even when it is not expressed 100% with both hands. Naturally, at such times, elements other than the hands—such as the distinctive facial expressions, eye movements, and the shape and movement of the mouth used in sign language—play a very important role.

Sometimes, a conversation can continue using not even one hand, but only facial expressions. For example, a single glance can express, “There’s that person over there / It’s that place over there,” or touching the inside of the cheek with the tongue can mean, “That’s a lie.” When both hands are occupied carrying things, a person can draw in their chin, raise their eyebrows, and stare at the other person to ask, “Really? / Huh?”, or open their mouth (“pa, pa”) while nodding to answer, “It’s finished.”

（※1）ふさがっている: Occupied / not free

（※2）何重にも: In many overlapping layers

（※3）織り込まれて: Woven or incorporated in multiple ways, like threads forming a pattern

（※4）チラリと: Briefly / for a moment

default.p.test-16-p1.vietnamese:
I imagine that many of our readers are very knowledgeable about economic issues, but did you know that there is a close relationship between clothing colors and the state of the economy?

Some time ago, I had the opportunity to see data collected over many years by a research institute. It examined the correlation between clothing colors and Japan’s economic conditions. Specifically, among people walking in the streets, when the proportion wearing black was high—even if they were not dressed entirely in black, as long as they wore at least one black item—the economy was in recession; when the proportion was low, the economy was flourishing.

In this column last February, I wrote, 'The economy will be in recession this year, so black will be popular,' and that proved to be true: last year’s fall and winter fashion was so dominated by black that it was almost completely taken over by the color 'black.' In fact, was not last fall and winter the peak of the psychological sense of recession? (A passage omitted)

As for the situation now, the fashion of young women with an extremely keen sense of style, known as 'gyaru,' has changed noticeably. Black has declined, while non-black colors such as white and beige, as well as floral patterns on white backgrounds, are increasing.

Many people may think that gyaru fashion and economic recession have little to do with each other, but that is not actually the case.

（※1）Dear readers: Our readers, fellow readers

（※2）Taken over by black: Becoming entirely black

（※3）Fashion consciousness: Paying close attention to fashion

default.p.test-17-p1.vietnamese:
In Japanese tradition, there is really no custom of arguing. Japanese people are not good at arguing. People generally believe that it is good for almost everyone to share the same opinion, and they tend to regard anyone with a different opinion as an enemy.

Japan’s community-oriented tradition has both good and bad sides. To cooperate in pursuing a shared goal, it is probably good not to insist only on one’s individual ego. On the other hand, people with different opinions are excluded from the community no matter what. It is very difficult to accept people with different opinions. When this becomes even more extreme, expressing an opinion itself becomes something that is not particularly welcome. That is why people do not argue. Whenever an argument occurs, there is a very strong tendency to divide people into enemies and allies. This is the negative side.

In European societies, people argue a great deal. In the United States, too, people argue more than in Japan. This can be seen everywhere. For example, when the BBC in the United Kingdom holds a talk-show-style discussion about any issue—not limited to politics—everyone brings a different opinion and debates quite intensely. Arguing here does not mean shouting in the other person’s face; it means developing one’s own reasoning and explaining that one thinks this way for reasons such as these. The opposing side does the same, and both sides present evidence to contend with each other’s positions. On Japanese television discussion programs, in general, either everyone says the same things or they turn to shouting at one another; it usually falls into one of these two situations.

(※1) Murahachibu: Excluding someone from a group and boycotting them from the community

(※2) Extreme: Far outside the ordinary range, biased toward one side

(※3) Talk-show discussion: A gathering where people sit together, talk, and exchange opinions

default.p.test-18-p1.vietnamese:
Like joy and sadness, anger is a basic human emotion, and its mechanisms and functions have long been studied. Recently, it has also gradually come to be viewed as a factor that harms human health. For example, according to a study examining the relationship between anger and heart disease, patients with heart disease accompanied by high blood pressure tend to have irritable personalities. There have also been reports that anger affects the nervous and immune systems, which may increase the risk of heart disease.

The relationship between anger and health may have begun to attract attention because society's view of illness has gradually changed. As the population ages, the medical costs borne by society as a whole have become impossible to ignore. Not only individual patients but also the medical expenses paid by the government and insurance companies have increased. To restrain this trend, disease prevention is of the utmost importance. Preventing illness by paying attention to lifestyle habits such as diet and sleep has long been widely recognized. In modern times, however, various research findings have also revealed that psychological factors, such as an individual's personality and patterns of thinking, affect health. For this reason, psychology and medicine have begun to examine the relationship between anger and health.

(※1) Immunity: The body's ability to automatically resist disease-causing bacteria when they enter the body.

(※2) Risk: The possibility of danger or harm

default.p.test-19-p1.outline.0.label: The current decline in the number of juvenile crimes
default.p.test-19-p1.outline.0.note: Cites the National Police Agency: the number of juvenile offenders has continued to decline, partly because of the falling birth rate.
default.p.test-19-p1.outline.1.label: A record-high increase in the recidivism rate
default.p.test-19-p1.outline.1.note: Points out the opposite reality: the recidivism rate has continued to rise and reached a record high because of association with delinquent groups and difficulty establishing a stable life.
default.p.test-19-p1.outline.2.label: The police's new policy: a proactive model for supporting teenagers' reintegration into society
default.p.test-19-p1.outline.2.note: The police shifted from their former passive attitude to proactive outreach, working with parents and volunteers to set goals, encourage the children, provide guidance, and help them turn their lives around.
default.p.test-19-p1.outline.3.label: Vocabulary notes and specialized terminology in the passage
default.p.test-19-p1.outline.3.note: Explains professional terms and phrases such as criminal offense, forwarding a case to the public prosecutor's office, falling into delinquency, and the proactive model.
default.p.test-19-p1.vietnamese:
According to the National Police Agency, the number of juveniles arrested or referred to prosecutors for criminal offenses has tended to decline in recent years. In 2009, it fell 0.8% from the previous year to 90,282. Partly because of the declining birthrate, this figure was only about half the peak recorded in 1983. On the other hand, however, the recidivism rate—the percentage of people who commit another offense—has continued to rise steadily since 1998, reaching a record high of 31.3% in 2009. It is reported that cases in which young people continue associating with delinquent groups, fail to establish stable lives, and fall back into delinquency are becoming increasingly prominent.

Until now, police stations only provided counseling when juveniles took the initiative to seek them out. From now on, however, they will change this passive approach and adopt an active policy of building relationships called the "outreach" model. For young people who still have unresolved problems and feel anxious about the future, juvenile officers at the local police station and local volunteers will proactively contact them with their parents' consent. After discussing matters with the parents, they will set goals such as "being able to attend school regularly without skipping classes" or "being able to continue working diligently." They will encourage the young people and provide counseling by telephone, email, or home visits. In addition, believing that the experience of being praised or appreciated by others can be a turning point toward rehabilitation, they will invite the young people to participate in volunteer activities such as picking up litter or visiting nursing homes.

(※1) Criminal offense: An offense that violates criminal law.

(※2) Refer a case to prosecutors: Send investigative records concerning a case to support its prosecution.

(※3) Fall into delinquency: For a juvenile to begin violating social rules or the law.

(※4) Be offered: Have one's story received or be approached.

(※5) Give something a name: Name or call something.

(※6) Change the policy: Change the objective or method.

(※7) Local police station: The police unit responsible for that area.

(※8) Visit to encourage: Visit someone to encourage them and lift their spirits.

The brilliant flowers displayed at flower shops delight our eyes, but what about the weeds growing along the roadside? Are they useless plants that cannot bring people any visual pleasure?

default.p.test-20-p1.outline.4.note: Summarizing the article's message: the brain does not take in every image that enters the eyes but actively filters out unnecessary information.
default.p.test-20-p1.vietnamese:
In fact, there are times when we fail to notice things that we cannot see. Failing to notice something we do not see is perfectly normal.

For example, consider the movement of your eyes as you read this book. When you move to the next line, it feels as though the passage continues seamlessly in your mind. Yet there is a gap between the end of one line and the beginning of the next. Where does that gap go?

When researchers actually measure eye movement while people read, they observe that the eyes slowly adjust to the reading speed while reading ordinary text, but at the point where the line changes, an extremely rapid eye movement called a saccade occurs.

The important point is that we cannot see the images entering our eyes during a saccade. If we could see them, the eyes would move so rapidly that we would probably feel sick before we could finish reading. Only the images during the saccade are omitted; the images before and after it are joined together so that we can see them.

In short, we do not see every image that enters our eyes.

default.p.test-21-p1.vietnamese:
Because I tend to think deeply about things, I often feel that life is exhausting and difficult.

I believe that the reason I, a person like this, am still living the way I am today is, without exaggeration, novels. For others, it may be a wonderful manga, theater, music, or film.

I have always lived by craving words as if I were hungry, taking those words into myself, reflecting on them in my own way, and protecting myself through language. This is not because I have any special talent for language or because I am particularly intelligent; it is because I read things I did not understand over and over again. When I was a student, I always pushed myself beyond my limits to encounter a wide range of works. I felt that if I did not do so, I would not be able to go on living.

Whenever I see news reports about students taking their own lives or people who have ended up choosing a path of self-destruction, I think about many things. I believe that feeling despair in life is also unavoidable. Not everyone can live cheerfully and optimistically. When one's family, friends, school, and workplace are all unable to offer any help, there is still something in this world called culture. Culture opens its doors equally to everyone. Although it is difficult to find in today's society because it is flooded with superficial products pursuing commercial profit, when we encounter something that deeply moves our souls and saves us, there will surely come a time when we think, “Maybe I should try living once more.”

（※1）Shindoi: feeling tired and distressed, exhausted

（※2）Hametsu (ruin): a person, life, family, country, etc. becoming completely ruined or falling apart

（※3）Commercially driven: intended to make a profit

（※4）To move deeply: to stir someone's emotions / move the soul

default.p.test-22-p1.vietnamese:
If you were asked why you were laughing, you would probably answer that it was because you found something funny. The ancient philosopher Aristotle once believed that only human beings could laugh. It seems that since ancient Greece, people have pointed out psychological benefits of laughter, such as improving one's mood.

If we consider laughter from a physical perspective rather than its psychological effects, laughter is produced when we inhale and exhale air, making it a phenomenon similar to breathing. In recent years, people have gradually come to understand that a similar phenomenon occurs not only in humans but also in primates (※1). When they chase one another or wrestle while playing, they sometimes open their mouths wide and bare their teeth at one another. ①Such behavior basically expresses an intention to attack, but in a play situation, it instead becomes a message indicating that there is no such intention.

However, human smiles differ from those of primates and have many diverse social meanings. For example, laughing at something funny the other person says is laughter that occurs within a relationship of connection with that person. Laughter expresses empathy (※2) with the other person and makes the atmosphere more cheerful. Some people also believe that the most primitive form of spoken language was laughter. If we think that laughter was used as a communication tool from the earliest stages of human history, just as it is today, this idea is not strange at all.

（※1）Primates: An animal classification that includes humans as well as monkeys and apes

（※2）Empathy: Feeling that another person's thoughts or emotions are the same as one's own, and feeling that they are truly so

default.p.test-23-p1.outline.0.label: Background: Abolition of subsidies and public reaction
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.0.note: The Environmental Bureau announces the abolition of subsidies for mountain toilets, prompting conflicting opinions from the parties involved.
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.1.label: Viewpoint A: Public responsibility and government subsidies
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.1.note: Person A asserts that mountain lodges have an extremely high public value because they ensure climbers' safety, and therefore require government financial support.
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.2.label: A’s view: environmental effects and a funding deficit.
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.2.note: A emphasizes that the growing number of mountain climbers will cause pollution without proper maintenance; visitor fees cannot cover the costs, so subsidies are essential.
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.3.label: View B: rejecting the idea of public provision and requiring users to pay for themselves
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.3.note: Author B argues that mountain toilets serve only climbers and belong to private businesses, so public funds should not be used and users must pay for themselves.
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.4.label: Viewpoint B: Proposals for alternatives to subsidies
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.4.note: B proposes promoting portable mini toilet bags and limiting the number of people allowed into the mountains instead of providing subsidies.
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.5.label: Notes on words in the passage
default.p.test-23-p1.outline.5.note: Definitions of the terms marked with asterisks in the question
default.p.test-23-p1.vietnamese:
On the 5th of last month, the Environmental Agency reviewed its projects and announced the abolition of the “Mountain Environmental Cleanup Project Subsidy,” a payment that supports the maintenance and improvement of toilets installed at mountain huts. In response to this move, various opinions were expressed by the parties concerned.

A
Although most mountain huts in Japan are operated by private businesses, I believe they have an extremely high degree of public importance. This is because mountain huts also perform roles directly related to hikers' safety, such as preventing accidents and maintaining mountain trails. For this reason, even when they are privately operated, government support is still essential.

In recent years, the number of hikers has continued to increase. Because the toilets are not properly maintained, used toilet paper is discarded carelessly in the mountains, creating a serious concern about the burden on the environment. Subsidies are absolutely necessary both to protect the mountain environment and to preserve its beautiful scenery.

Some people argue that users should pay for environmental cleanup themselves. However, if the work relies solely on the toilet fees hikers have paid up to now, there will always be a deficit, leaving no surplus at all for repairing the toilets. Considering the negative effects on valuable mountain vegetation and the risk of polluting rivers and other water sources caused by poorly maintained toilets, I hope everyone will reconsider the fact that mountains are a precious asset belonging to the entire nation.

B
Toilets in town parks are public facilities, but is it really necessary to recognize the public importance of toilets in remote and rugged mountain areas, where they are used only by hikers? Moreover, most mountain huts are operated by private businesses, so directing national funds toward them is completely unreasonable.

The only people who benefit from maintaining toilets at mountain huts are the hikers who use them. Therefore, the user-pays principle should be thoroughly applied by collecting fees from users.

Environmental conservation is necessary, but instead of providing subsidies, we should focus our efforts on new projects that promote the use of portable toilet bags. There are surely other feasible measures as well, such as limiting the number of people allowed to enter the mountains each day.

(※1) Project: A large-scale undertaking carried out for the benefit of society

(※2) Mountainous region: An area containing many high and rugged mountain ranges

(※3) Subsidy: Money provided by the national or prefectural government to support activities of a public nature

(※4) Vegetation: A community of plants growing together in a particular area

(※5) Investment / allocating funds: Using money or human resources to achieve a particular purpose

(※6) Portable mini toilet: An item resembling a waste container that allows people to carry their waste home after using the toilet

default.p.test-24-p1.vietnamese:
A
The work 『R』 was lavishly praised by readers from the time it was serialized in the monthly magazine 『Bungei Iroha』, and was eventually published as a complete three-volume book set.

The story begins with a secret agreement between Japan and the United States behind the negotiations for Okinawa's reversion. The Foreign Ministry official who leaked the information and the newspaper reporter who received it were subsequently prosecuted.

Drawing on a large volume of testimony and documents gathered through a lengthy investigative process, this work recreates in meticulous detail the hidden worlds of politics and newspaper offices. It is a masterpiece that fully—and even more than—satisfies readers' desire to know the truth. In addition, the characters' psychological changes and the scenery of Okinawa are portrayed with extraordinary vividness, powerfully drawing readers into the world of the novel.

B
The work 『R』—the author's first long novel after a long absence—also became a bestseller. It was also decided that the work would be adapted into a television drama the following spring.

The secret agreement between Japan and the United States at the time of Okinawa's reversion was brought to public attention through the main character, a newspaper reporter. What began as a diplomatic issue gradually developed into a relationship between the journalist and the source of the information.

Reading this book, a work based on thorough investigative reporting and a wealth of research materials, I was deeply moved by the author's determination to pursue the truth. Okinawa is also my hometown, and the main character's occupation as a newspaper reporter felt especially familiar to me as a journalist. The scenes seemed to appear before my eyes, and the tense atmosphere felt so real that it was almost tangible. However, it is truly regrettable that the depiction of the Okinawa reversion scene is overly ordinary and formulaic.

（※1）Serialized: Continuously published in a newspaper or magazine over a period of time

（※2）Lavishly praised: Described as extremely excellent; highly acclaimed

（※3）Standalone book edition: A book published independently, rather than as part of a magazine or regular series

（※4）Reversion: The act of returning something to its original place or owner

（※5）Secret agreement: A confidential agreement

default.p.test-25-p1.vietnamese:
A (Newspaper)
Bike-sharing service launched in Maruyama City
A bike-sharing project offering electric-bike rentals began on October 1 through cooperation between the shopping district in front of Maruyama Station and ABC, an electric-bicycle manufacturer. Users who pay a one-time registration fee of 500 yen and a regular annual membership fee of 5,000 yen can use an electric bicycle for 200 yen per two hours. Since the area around this shopping district has many steep slopes, demand for electric-bicycle rentals is expected to be strong in the future.

In addition, bicycle parking stations have been placed approximately 500 meters apart within a 4-kilometer radius centered on the shopping district.

The shopping district provides discount coupons usable in the district to members in order to attract customers.

B (Magazine)
Shared bicycle service “Bye Bye Bicycle” launched in Shirakawa City
Shirakawa City has established bicycle parking stations at 20 locations throughout the city and prepared 200 bicycles for rental. After use, bicycles may be returned to any bicycle parking station. This is a new environmental project intended to reduce the number of cars traveling through the city and cut CO₂ emissions.

The initial costs and the first year's operating and management costs will be subsidized by the national government. From the second year onward, operating and management costs will be covered by usage fees and advertising revenue from advertisements displayed at the parking stations.

To use the service, users must pay a one-time registration fee of 1,000 yen and a monthly membership fee of 300 yen. Bicycle use is free for the first hour, after which it costs 100 yen for every two hours. Because the service is relatively inexpensive, the number of users is expected to increase and the business is expected to expand in the future.

(*1) Share: for people to use something together

(*2) Project/undertaking: a major undertaking carried out for society

(*3) Operate: to make an organization or rules function effectively

(*4) Cover costs: to make things work with limited money or personnel

default.p.test-26-p1.vietnamese:
Some people say that they do not know how to look at photographs or what makes a photograph good. What they mean is that perhaps there is some kind of “measuring stick” for evaluating a work, and that applying it would tell them whether their photograph is good or bad.

There are generally three ways to convey what one has seen to others: “speaking,” “communicating through writing,” and “communicating through images.” At first glance, they may seem to be separate methods, but in fact, whether we are speaking or reading a text, the content appears in our minds as images. The images in our minds continually change as the content and manner of expression in speech or writing change. Whether speaking aloud or reading each written character, we are making ourselves imagine images. With photographs, the reverse happens: photographs allow us to perceive words and speech through the image itself.

When the author encounters a photograph that seems “wonderful” at a photography exhibition, in a newspaper, or in a magazine, the author always feels that they are not looking at a photograph but are actually present in the space recorded by it. Rather than appreciating it from a distance as something photographed by someone else, the author imagines standing at the scene and witnessing the view personally. In this way, the author even imagines the voices of the people in the frame, the surrounding sounds, the smells, and the sensation of touching objects.

If we simply regard a photograph as a two-dimensional world on a sheet of paper and move on, it becomes dull and tasteless. But if we try to immerse ourselves in the image, it becomes alive, as though it were breathing. When we feel that a photograph is beautiful, we should become like a ninja sneaking deep into the work, or transform into Sun Wukong or Doraemon and fly freely through that space and time.

A photograph records a real moment that once occurred. It takes us directly to fascinating landscapes or human living spaces that we have never seen before. When we open an old album and become absorbed in a photograph taken with our grandparents, it feels as though we have returned to childhood and can hear our grandparents' voices echoing again.

Could a beautiful photograph be one that makes us want to step into the world appearing within it, or one that makes us unconsciously forget ourselves, become absorbed in conversing with the photograph, and seem to hear words coming from inside the frame?

（※1）Association: imagining or recalling related things

（※2）Tactile sensation: the feeling produced by touching something with the hand or making contact with the skin

（※3）Two-dimensional: extending only in length and width, rather than having a three-dimensional solid form

（※4）Dull and tasteless: boring and lacking anything interesting

（※5）Forget oneself: become so absorbed or captivated that one is no longer conscious of oneself

default.p.test-27-p1.vietnamese:
When you search online for the phrase “book review essay,” countless ready-made reviews appear in bundles. Some websites classify them carefully by level, such as “for elementary school students,” “for junior and senior high school students,” and “for university students.” Others make it easy to find classic works such as “Bocchan,” “Rashomon,” and “Kokoro” (※1). You can simply copy one word for word and your essay is finished. These sites even thoughtfully include a warning: “If you are found out, you are responsible for the consequences.”

For students who feel guilty and hesitate (①) to submit a word-for-word copy to their school, there are “templates” with blank spaces ( ) where they can enter their own thoughts. There is even an “easy order” option, an “automatic generator” (software that generates text (※2)), which completes the essay automatically after the student answers a few questions, such as the title of the book.

It seems that this world has even carefully anticipated students being caught copying text from the Internet and reprimanded by their teachers. If you continue searching in the spirit of “even a stray dog sometimes finds food” (※3), you will come across (※4) websites offering “reflection reports” for cases in which students are caught copying and pasting. There are sample statements such as “I promise never to repeat such a careless/wrong act (※5) again,” along with advice to write the report by “changing the order, replacing the wording, and editing it.” Although I thought this was merely an excessive joke, faced with such thorough attention to every last detail (※6), I could only express my amazement.

（A section omitted）

Even though these are only students’ book reviews, the teachers grading them are also being tested. Evaluating the quality of the writing alone is already difficult; determining whether an essay was copied and pasted from the Internet must be an extraordinarily challenging task (※7).

Apparently, many teachers can no longer casually say, “Well done,” and a university professor eventually came up with “copy-and-paste detection software.” The software is said to check whether students’ reports or theses have been copied from online texts. When digitized text is entered into the software, it scans the Internet for copied material and assesses whether the entire text or only part of it was copied, giving a specific percentage, such as 90%. Having this tool greatly reduces the effort required for checking.

However, when a submitted essay is identified as copied and pasted, the teachers are then faced with the challenge of deciding how to deal with that student.

After that, needless to say, websites offering ways to “defeat copy-and-paste detection software” will surely appear among the students, and a new endless cycle of countermeasures and counter-countermeasures will begin. ②

（※1）“Bocchan,” “Rashomon,” and “Kokoro”: These are all novel titles.

（※2）Generate: to create an object or product.

（※3）“A dog out for a walk”: This resembles the proverb “Even a dog out for a walk may eventually run into a stick,” meaning that if you keep taking action, you may sometimes get lucky.

（※4）Come across: to find something by chance.

（※5）Wrong/careless act: Trouble or a problem caused by careless or irresponsible behavior that inconveniences others.

（※6）Thorough attention to every detail: A state in which every aspect is carefully considered and attended to.

（※7）Extraordinarily challenging task: Something extremely difficult to accomplish.

default.p.test-28-p1.outline.0.label: The current state of food disposal and the solution proposed by the Consumer Affairs Agency.
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.0.note: Japan discards large amounts of food approaching its expiration date. The Consumer Affairs Agency believes this is because people do not understand expiration labels and is therefore conducting an awareness campaign.
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.1.label: The author's counterargument: Publicity alone is not enough
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.1.note: Points out that about 80% of people already understand expiration dates correctly, so publicity alone cannot solve the problem.
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.2.label: The real reason and the mechanism for categorizing choices by price
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.2.note: Near-expiration products do not sell because they are priced the same as fresh products; discounting them would give consumers more choices (basis for Questions 1 and 2).
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.3.label: Businesses' passivity and rebuttals to concerns about price reductions
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.3.note: Companies hesitate to discount products because they fear harming their brands and are concerned about safety, but the author argues that mass disposal conflicts with their social responsibility.
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.4.label: Conclusion and position: direct price reductions instead of destroying products
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.4.note: The author proposes that the Consumer Affairs Agency instruct businesses to discount products before destroying them (evidence for Question 3).

default.p.test-28-p1.vietnamese:
In Japan, a country with a low food self-sufficiency rate of only 40%, large quantities of returned food are being discarded simply because the best-before date is approaching (※1), even though the food is still safe to eat. The Consumer Affairs Agency believes that unsold food results from consumers’ failure to understand the meaning of expiration-date labels or from their excessive concern about freshness (※2). It therefore plans to conduct awareness campaigns (※3) to promote the idea that food can still be eaten after the date and to change consumers’ attitudes.

However, I believe that this alone will not be enough to reduce the amount of food being destroyed. According to some surveys, approximately 80% of people already understand the precise meaning of the date label and know that eating food after that date does not pose a health problem.

Why do foods approaching their best-before dates remain unsold? In my view, the reason is that products nearing their dates and products with plenty of time remaining are sold at the same price. If the prices are the same, it is perfectly natural for consumers who care about freshness to choose the slightly fresher product—in other words, the one with more time remaining before its best-before date. On the other hand, if products nearing their dates are discounted, consumers can choose between a fresh product at the regular price and a slightly less fresh product at a lower price. (A section has been omitted.)

①Although discounting would reduce the amount of food left unsold as its best-before date approaches, manufacturers and retailers are reluctant to do so. Under the current system, out of concern for consumer safety, products nearing their dates are not sold but returned or destroyed. However, since food can still be eaten after the date, there would be no problem with selling those products. Even if health problems arose because consumers failed to store and manage the food properly after purchasing it, that would be the responsibility of the consumers themselves. There is also the view that if discounting became a regular practice (※4), fewer consumers would buy products at the listed price and the brand image would suffer. Nevertheless, from the standpoint of corporate social responsibility, continuing to destroy large quantities of food is highly undesirable.

At present, manufacturers and retailers make no effort to find ways to sell food nearing its best-before date; instead, they return or destroy it. However, if consumers were given the authority to decide whether to buy it (※5), the amount of unsold stock would certainly decrease, and the amount of food destroyed could also be reduced. Therefore, the Consumer Affairs Agency should instruct manufacturers and retailers to discount these products before returning or destroying them, allowing consumers to buy food at lower prices.

（※1）Best-before date: the date indicating the period during which food is expected to taste its best

（※2）Being overly particular: being excessively concerned about something

（※3）Awareness campaign: teaching people about things they have not recognized and improving their understanding and knowledge

（※4）Becoming customary: becoming commonplace or taken for granted

（※5）Entrusting the decision: allowing someone else to decide or handle something

default.p.test-29-p1.outline.0.label: The Tower of Babel legend and its explanation for linguistic diversity
default.p.test-29-p1.outline.0.note: Begins with the legend of the Tower of Babel: humanity once shared one language and planned to build a tower to heaven, so God confused their speech. The author explains that the story was created to account for why humanity has many languages today.
default.p.test-29-p1.outline.1.label: The inconvenience of multilingualism and efforts to create the common language Esperanto
default.p.test-29-p1.outline.1.note: The passage presents the usual view that linguistic diversity creates major inconveniences for communication and travel, leading to the idea of unifying speech through the creation of an artificial language such as Esperanto.
default.p.test-29-p1.outline.2.label: A positive perspective: linguistic diversity creates a rich culture and awareness of other people.
default.p.test-29-p1.outline.2.note: Reverses the issue: it is precisely because languages are divided that human culture is so diverse. This enables us to deeply recognize the “absolute other”—people with different ideas and beliefs—and nurtures the desire to understand them.
default.p.test-29-p1.outline.3.label: The author's position: the positive value of linguistic diversity
default.p.test-29-p1.outline.3.note: The author affirms the central idea that although language differences are inconvenient, they give people opportunities to learn new languages and become fascinated by other cultures.

default.p.test-29-p1.vietnamese:
Originally, everyone around the world spoke the same language. To prevent humanity from becoming scattered across the earth, people conceived the idea of building a tower reaching up to the heavens as a symbol of unity. This was the Tower of Babel.

However, God thought that people were making such plans because they all spoke the same language. If they were left alone, who knew what outrageous and reckless things they might do? So God confused their language so that they could no longer understand one another. That is the story. As I explained at the beginning, there are more than 3,000 languages in the world, and perhaps this story was invented to explain why languages became so fragmented and dispersed.

Indeed, it is strange, and also extremely inconvenient, that such diverse languages are used according to region. If one language were shared throughout the world, we could talk with anyone wherever we went, and traveling abroad would be easy and comfortable. Many people have probably thought how convenient that would be. In fact, you may know that, based on this concept or ideal, people once attempted to create an artificial language called Esperanto as a common language for the entire world.

However, could we not also consider the matter from the opposite perspective? If only one language existed in the world, would cultures really have developed with such variety, appeal, and richness? Is it not precisely because languages are scattered and diverse that the world has developed such colorful and distinctive cultures? And is it not through contact with those cultures that we first turn our attention to the obvious and unchanging fact that people with values, customs, ideas, and beliefs different from our own—in other words, “absolutely different others” (the absolute other ①)—live everywhere in the world, allowing us to be genuinely astonished and to become humble from the depths of our hearts? Furthermore, does this not allow us to nurture a sincere and passionate desire to talk with and understand such people?

In short, because the Tower of Babel collapsed, people around the world had to speak different languages and were placed in the inconvenient situation of being unable to communicate easily. On the other hand, this also gave us the opportunity to learn unfamiliar languages and, through them, to develop a passion and interest in other cultures. Should we not try to think of it in that way?

(※1) Doing something outrageous: Going far beyond the bounds of ordinary standards

(※2) Doing something terrible: Accidentally doing something horrifying

(※3) Concept / ideal: A basic idea of how things ought to be

(※4) Strict / obvious and unchanging: Strict and impossible to change

(※5) Turn one's attention toward: Direct one's interest toward distant things

(※6) Sincere / passionate: Felt strongly because the matter is close and significant

(※7) Collapse: Failing or coming to nothing

Evacuation preparation information

This is the Aoba City Disaster Prevention Headquarters.

Because the Sakuragawa River has risen due to localized heavy rain since last night, there is a risk of flooding.

For this reason, evacuation preparation information was issued for the Sakuradai area at 11:20. Please begin preparing to evacuate so that you can leave at any time. In addition, please remind your neighbors if possible.

◎ Older people and others who need more time to evacuate should evacuate immediately to Sakuradai Elementary School.

Please also note that the Sakuragawa Kaido route is currently closed to traffic. To reach Sakuradai Elementary School, do not use a car; travel on foot via a detour in the direction of Asahicho.

Aoba City Disaster Prevention Headquarters
1234-5678
saigai@aoba.or.jp

default.p.test-33-p1.vietnamese:
The expression "vulnerable to natural disasters" means that when a disaster occurs, it causes extensive damage and its effects continue for a long time. Let us think about why we become vulnerable to natural disasters. First, one reason is that the larger a disaster is, the less frequently it occurs. Although houses and cities should be built to withstand disasters, people inadvertently forget about disasters.

For example, suppose we build a new house. In our country, once a house has been built, people generally do not take the initiative to care for or maintain it. They make repairs only when roof tiles are blown away by a storm or heavy rain causes flooding and the plaster on the walls to fall off. In short, unless the house leaks or visible damage appears, people do not repair it. Therefore, in our country, the older a house becomes, the more quickly its real-estate value declines. At the same time, the house becomes increasingly vulnerable to natural disasters.

default.p.test-33-p10.vietnamese:
A

The author conducted an experiment in this novel. Specifically, the experiment involved changing the writing style. Until now, the author had used a familiar style that allowed readers to feel as if they were gently stepping from everyday life into the world of the novel. In this novel, however, the author uses many archaic and stiff expressions, creating an atmosphere that almost makes readers forget that the story is set in modern times. Readers may be surprised by this change, but the author's storytelling ability remains unchanged and never makes them feel bored.

This story contains many passages that seem to foreshadow a continuation, making it difficult to believe that it will end in this single volume. Although expectations for the next installment continue to grow, I also feel that it would be perfectly acceptable even if there were no sequel. Readers can appreciate the ending of the story according to their own interpretations.

B

This novel deals with so many diverse themes that it is difficult to introduce it briefly. The protagonist is an ordinary young man working for an ordinary company. He becomes involved in a financial-trading scandal that shocks society. In addition to his work, he faces other problems, and his inner changes as he confronts conflicts with his parents, the death of his best friend, his lover's illness, and so on are gradually portrayed in detail.

The author has poured into this novel everything he has pursued through his efforts up to now. The work delivers a powerful message that the human spirit is not controlled by social pressure. What concerns me is that part of the story clearly remains unfinished. Although the publisher has made no official announcement, I believe the sequel to this novel has already been written. I would like a proper evaluation of this novel to be made after the final part of the story is published.

(*1) Talent: The ability to carry something out.

(*2) Be drawn into an incident: Be forced to become involved in an incident against one's wishes.

default.p.test-33-p11.vietnamese:
People often say that “work exists to ensure survival and put food on the table,” but the same is true of animals other than humans: they also search for food in order to survive. Humans are said to differ from other animals in that they live together in groups called society. However, this is not limited to monkeys, elephants, and birds; many insects, such as ants and bees, also live collectively. Therefore, social living alone cannot distinguish humans from other animals.

Even if we focus on the formation of society, at a primitive level there was hardly any difference from a troop of monkeys.

However, by walking on two legs, humans freed their forelimbs. In other words, they gained hands, and with them they could turn natural objects into tools. Moreover, using their own hands, humans were able to improve those tools and create new tools from new materials. This process—the ability to make tools—is thought to have created a clear difference and drawn a distinct boundary between humans and other animals. Monkeys can use objects around them as tools, but they cannot make tools themselves.

And this is the important point. Thanks to tools, humans could not only feed themselves and their children but also support elderly parents who were no longer able to work—in other words, who could no longer obtain food for themselves. Caring for parents is precisely what makes humans decisively different from other animals.

Of course, in the past, the long life expectancy we have today was not guaranteed, so most people basically died through natural causes once they reached an age at which they could no longer work. Even so, it seems that humans had, from a very long time ago, a society in which elderly people who had lost their productive capacity could continue living alongside others. In other words, by using and developing tools, humans became able to produce a surplus, allowing not only producers and their successors but also others to survive. This made it possible for elderly parents to continue living.

(Section omitted)

The concept of occupations and labor has appeared only recently in the long course of human history. From this perspective, a society in which people with no productive capacity, or with insufficient productive capacity, can still live may be the ideal society that humanity has sought for so many years. I hate pain. This is because pain is not merely physical discomfort or suffering; it also has a tremendous effect on a person's mind.

The medical view up to now has been: since treatment is meant to restore health, one should endure a little pain. In less compassionate medical settings, there have even been cases in which the patient's pain itself was ignored.

The idea that “since it is medical treatment, pain is only natural” has quietly become common sense without anyone having to say it out loud. (A passage has been omitted.) However, the truth is that suffering can sometimes cause a person's mind to collapse and break down. Pain not only damages the body; it also distorts the human mind and soul. That is why I hate pain.

default.p.test-33-p4.vietnamese:
Dear Mr. Handa (salutation omitted), regarding the matter I was cautioned about the other day, my careless behavior caused you, the landlord, a great deal of inconvenience. I also feel deeply sorry and guilty for causing discomfort to the neighbors. I sincerely apologize from the bottom of my heart.

In a one-room apartment where even the slightest sound of footsteps can be irritating to the ears, I gave no thought whatsoever to how much inconvenience a noisy gathering of many people late at night would cause the neighbors. I am deeply ashamed and am reflecting seriously on my behavior.

From now on, I will never make noise or create loud sounds in my room again. I will also limit the number of people I invite over, and whenever I have guests, I will always take care and be considerate of the neighbors around me.

I humbly ask that you forgive me for this careless and irresponsible incident.

Sincerely,

April 5, Heisei 23 (2011)

Jun Takahashi

default.p.test-33-p6.vietnamese:
Between 2000 and 2001, major national newspapers changed their standard type size to one that was slightly larger. I think local newspapers did something similar. Although the increase in the elderly population was probably one reason, this was because the proportion of newspaper readers who needed reading glasses had increased.

The press also considers “the customer to be king,” so it is only natural to change the layout of a newspaper according to the king’s needs. In the announcement, the old and new typefaces were compared to show clearly and convincingly how much easier the new type was to read. I also think that most editorial offices wrote something similar: because the page size would not change, “the more the type size increases, the more the number of words must be reduced; therefore, articles will focus on the main points, be streamlined, and aim for greater efficiency.” On the one hand, I found this very reasonable; on the other, I wondered whether articles had not been streamlined in this way before.

Large-print books have also begun circulating widely on the market. In particular, dictionaries have been released in large-format editions with the same content and design, and readers have welcomed them because they can look things up without reading glasses. However, as their size increases, they also become bulky and heavy. For people who find their convenience and comfort indispensable, though, this is not a problem.

default.p.test-33-p7.vietnamese:
When I worked as a zookeeper, I no longer needed to draw “animal pictures for myself.” Zookeepers form bonds with animals so deep that ordinary people can hardly imagine them. We clean, prepare food, care for their bodies, observe them, treat them when they are sick, and perform autopsies when they die. We are constantly covered in feces and smeared with blood.

(Part omitted)

I did not actually hold a pencil and draw in a sketchbook. However, I watched them countless times, as though tracing every line with my eyes. Whatever the subject, when people draw, they look closely at its shape, color, texture, and so on. Just as I would use a brush to paint, I observed the animals from many different angles and drew them with my own eyes. By coming into contact with animals in this way, ①the animals seemed to enter my body through direct, physical sensation. That is why I no longer needed to draw. When I was aspiring to become an artist, I always tried to draw as many pictures as possible, thinking that this was the shortest path to improvement. But I was different at that time. Even without time to draw, I did not mind; on the contrary, I felt that I was learning “how to draw” even more than by actually sketching and drawing.

(※1) 目でなぞるように: as though tracing it with one’s eyes

(※2) 凝視する: to stare intently

default.p.test-33-p8.vietnamese:
We absorb oxygen from the air by breathing. Without oxygen, we would suffocate (※1) and die. Oxygen is essential for maintaining life. However, not many people know that oxygen is actually also a toxic substance harmful to our bodies.

With only a small trigger, oxygen changes into what is called “active oxygen.” Because of the word “active,” people may imagine that it works positively for our bodies, but in reality it is a troublesome substance (※2) with highly aggressive and toxic properties. Active oxygen is believed to be the real culprit behind various phenomena associated with aging. (A section has been omitted.)

Although oxygen is necessary to sustain life, using oxygen is precisely what causes us to age. In other words, we grow old because we breathe. Breathing itself is one of the causes of aging and death, and as long as we are alive, aging cannot be avoided. What an irony.

It appears that aging is also slowed when less oxygen is consumed. For example, some data show that people living in high-altitude regions, where oxygen is thin (※3), have a higher rate of longevity, and that restricting calories by eating until one is 80 percent full slows the aging process.

（※1）Suffocation: Being unable to breathe any longer

（※2）Troublesome substance: Something troublesome or bothersome

（※3）Thin: Sparse, low in concentration

default.p.test-33-p9.vietnamese:
Since ancient times, people have always depended on nature’s many blessings to survive. Moreover, humans have not merely lived amid nature; they have also altered it by cultivating fields, raising animals, and building towns in order to create living environments for themselves. It can be said that, up to a certain point in history, human exploitation and development had not affected nature on such a large scale. However, with the development of industry from the eighteenth century onward, human activities carried out for our own benefit began to severely disrupt that balance. Today, people face the urgent need to live while also considering the preservation and conservation of nature.

For this reason, interest in learning about the ecological behavior of the diverse plants and animals living on Earth has recently grown rapidly. To protect nature’s richness, we need to gain a deep understanding of how nature works—for example, which organisms live where and how they interact with one another. However, knowledge alone is not enough to preserve nature. For instance, even when an animal species is at risk of extinction, it may not be easy for humans to use their knowledge to predict and prevent that outcome. Understanding is certainly the first step toward protecting the environment. Nevertheless, we must not assume that this alone is sufficient; what is important is to face nature with a humble attitude.

default.p.test-34-p10.vietnamese:
Person seeking advice:

My husband suddenly said that he wants to become a dentist. Apparently, he wants to quit his current job and return to university. He says that he already has enough savings for this.

It is not that my husband's current job is going badly or that he dislikes it, so I was very surprised and wondered why he had only now brought this up. Moreover, I have heard that even if someone becomes a dentist these days, there is no guarantee of finding a job, so I am worried. However, I also feel that he will not regret doing work he loves, and part of me wants to support him.

Respondent: A (Dentist)

As you said, there is currently an oversupply of dentists. There is no guarantee that he will find a job in the area he wants, and the examination to become a dentist is far from easy, so even if he graduates from university, he may not pass on his first attempt. Furthermore, even if he has savings, there will certainly be financial worries. In such circumstances, can you continue supporting him for many years? I think his thinking is naive and unrealistic. If there is no problem with his current job, wouldn't it be better for him to continue working there?

Respondent: B (Lawyer)

So he has been saving money to return to university. I think that is wonderful. But why did he suddenly say that he wanted to become a dentist? You probably wish he had discussed it with you when he first started saving money, don't you? Why not ask him why he kept the savings a secret? Even if he has thought carefully about the future, the fact that he secretly saved money behind your back is reason enough for you to feel uneasy. Tell him honestly how you feel and try to have a thorough discussion with each other.

default.p.test-34-p11.vietnamese:
The third key to reading comprehension is background knowledge about the content of the text. This includes knowledge directly related to the subject of the text, such as politics, economics, society, science, sports, and the arts. Background knowledge of this kind has hardly ever been addressed in Japanese language classes up to now.

If we strictly follow the principle of 「eliminating preconceptions when reading a text」, having prior knowledge about the content of the writing is not only unnecessary but becomes an obstacle that prevents objective and logical understanding. Among reference books for modern Japanese, some confidently claim that logical thinking ability alone is sufficient and that knowledge of the text's content is unnecessary.

It is true that modern Japanese tests are intended to assess pure 「Japanese language ability」, such as reading comprehension and the ability to express the content of a text, so requiring background knowledge related to the content may be considered an unorthodox approach. However, reading a text without any prior knowledge at all is impossible. Even if we intend to eliminate it, preconceptions will somehow find their way in.

Suppose someone had absolutely no prior knowledge or preconceptions. That person would not even understand where the view expressed in the text stands—for example, whether it is an extreme opinion or a moderate one—and in the end, nothing in the text would remain in their mind.

In this sense, what is truly necessary is not 「reading while eliminating preconceptions」 but 「reading with a balanced preconception」. However, once it is balanced, it is no longer a 「preconception」, so the expression 「balanced preconception」 is actually contradictory. Nevertheless, this is what the author means.

There are various lines of argument surrounding many different issues. After understanding them as concrete knowledge, we ①temporarily set that knowledge aside and approach the question with the mindset of eliminating preconceptions. In this way, we can achieve ②a genuine understanding of the content of the text—something that cannot be achieved by relying solely on formal logical thinking ability. That is what I mean.

Naturally, the knowledge required differs depending on the subject of the text. Nevertheless, whether we are reading an editorial or commentary in a newspaper or magazine, or a specialized paperback or general-knowledge book, the background knowledge required in situations that call for 「reading comprehension」 as people living in modern society can, in one sentence, be summarized as an understanding of 「the modern era」.

default.p.test-34-p3.vietnamese:
Marketing management is not a simple job that can be handled easily. Even if business executives or marketing managers want to do things in a particular way, the market—that is, consumers and customers—does not move according to their wishes. A new product into which many resources have been invested may unfortunately fail, while a product launched after imitating a competitor may become a major hit. A campaign that takes a great deal of time and effort may fail, while quiet word-of-mouth among consumers may save the product. Things that go against expectations happen constantly. This is the biggest difference between management focused inward on the organization and management focused outward on the market. In other words, having to face a market that does not operate according to the wishes of executives or marketers is the source of the difficulty in marketing management.

Professor Yanaka's group fed pollen-allergic mice (※1) about 10 grams of bananas every day for three weeks and compared them with mice fed ordinary food. default.p.test-34-p6.vietnamese:
At museums, a wide variety of objects from ancient times to the present, from all over the world, are displayed. The way people appreciate them probably depends on the individual, but whenever I stand in front of an exhibit, I feel as though I am traveling back to the era in which it was used.

Thoughts arise in my mind about how these objects were originally used and where they were kept. If they are handicrafts that were used in daily life, it is easier to imagine even the small details. For example, if it is a thick, somber-looking tea bowl, who used it, and how? I can immediately picture an elegant tea gathering attended by people of high social standing. If it is a large vase decorated with beautiful paintings, what magnificent mansion once displayed it? If it is a kimono woven with intricate patterns, what kind of person wore it? Exhibits lead us, the people admiring them, into another world.

The more often I visited museums, the more I felt that simply looking at the exhibits was no longer satisfying. For example, why is a snowflake pattern depicted on that painted plate? The craftsperson must have put some intention into it. Later, I learned that snow symbolizes good fortune. Without understanding things like this, we cannot even imagine the thoughts of the people who used that painted plate in that era. For this reason, I began buying explanatory books sold at museums and reading them, and I started visiting libraries to learn more.

(※1) Ancient and modern, East and West: From ancient times to the present, from every region

(※2) Good fortune: A sign that something good is about to happen

default.p.test-34-p7.vietnamese:
When modern people are recognized as individuals with names rather than anonymous members of a crowd, their self-esteem is satisfied because they feel that their presence is respected and that they are valued.

Many stores train their employees to “Call customers by name.” Because employees learn customers’ names when they use a credit card or membership card, the store’s policy from then on is not to call them 「Customer」but to use their names, such as「Customer 〇〇」. (Middle section omitted)

When the author pays by credit card at the checkout counter, hearing an employee say「Thank you for always shopping with us, Ms. Kobayashi」makes her feel as if she has become a VIP regular customer and gives her a slight sense of superiority. When an employee who has served me, although I did not know her name, addresses me by name, I suddenly feel a sense of familiarity and closeness, and begin to feel warmly fond of her.

However, there are also times when I feel uncomfortable being called by name. Unlike female office workers who mainly shop at night or on Saturdays and Sundays, I go to the shopping center near my home regardless of the day or time. Around noon on a weekday, when an employee who recognizes me sees me, she starts talking:「Oh~ Ms. Kobayashi, what brings you here at this hour? Are you off today?」. I have no intention of standing beside the escalator and explaining my work circumstances, so I become flustered and embarrassed. I can only timidly wish that they would stop at「Hello, Ms. Kobayashi」, and on weekday daytime visits I make my way to the store feeling nervous and apprehensive.

(※1) Self-esteem: A feeling of valuing and respecting oneself

(※2) VIP customer: An important customer to the store

(※3) Sense of superiority: The feeling that one is superior to other people

(※4) Familiar face: Someone whose face one recognizes because one often sees them

(※5) Flustered: A state of losing one’s composure and becoming panicked

default.p.test-34-p8.vietnamese:
The web of the Jorō spider appears to be white whenever it is active during the day. Moreover, in autumn, depending on the intensity of sunlight, the radial threads appear slightly yellowish. However, even when looking at the delicate threads of a spider web, it is difficult to distinguish their exact color. Therefore, to confirm what color they actually are, researchers decided to examine the color of dragline silk secreted from the same gland as the radial threads.

When they examined the visible-light absorption spectra of a large quantity of collected dragline silk, they found that the silk was white from spring through summer, while the Jorō spider developed from a juvenile into an adult. However, when the spider reached adulthood in autumn, the silk clearly displayed a golden-yellow color. The reason the Jorō spider's web turns yellow is thought to be that it may serve as camouflage when the surrounding environment changes to autumn foliage. In other words, because the web resembles the colors around it, insects cannot notice it and are more easily caught. In contrast, a survey of the dragline silk of the nocturnal Zugro-onigumo spider found that it remained white from spring through autumn. This is thought to be because color is unnecessary for the nocturnal Zugro-onigumo spider.

(※1) Gland: an organ that produces or secretes substances

(※2) Secreted: released

(※3) Dragline silk: a spider's silk thread

(※4) Visible light: light that can be seen with the naked eye

(※5) Absorption spectrum: a graph showing the absorption of light

(※6) Juvenile: an organism that has not developed enough to reproduce

(※7) Adult: an organism that has developed enough to reproduce

default.p.test-34-p9.vietnamese:
This is something I experienced myself: because of my work, I often examine, read, and copy old documents from the Edo period (※1) from all over the country. Recently, however, I suddenly began wondering why I am able to understand documents from as far away as Kyushu.

It happened about four or five years ago, when I had the opportunity to visit Kagoshima (※2). While waiting at a bus stop for about five minutes, I noticed two elderly people beside me chatting cheerfully about all kinds of things. Curious about what they were talking about, I unintentionally listened carefully, trying to understand them, but I could not understand what they were saying at all. Of course, I could understand a few individual words, but I was completely unable to follow the context that explained why they were having such an enjoyable conversation.

That experience suddenly overlapped with my experience of reading old documents, making me feel that it was truly strange that I could understand documents from all over the country.

（Omitted section）

In other words, Japanese society has an extremely high degree of uniformity (※3) in its literate society and written world. In contrast, non-literate society and the oral world are far more diverse than we tend to think. Therefore, once the outer shell of this uniform literate society is peeled away, an extremely diverse folk-cultural society (※4) can be seen underneath.

① Contemporary Japanese society is by no means homogeneous either.

（※1）Edo period: the era from 1603 to 1867

（※2）Kagoshima: a place located on the island of Kyushu

（※3）Uniformity: the condition in which all parts have the same characteristics

（※4）Folk-cultural society: a society with distinctive customs and everyday culture

Could the prerequisite for an excellent short story be a good opening? The opening of this work,「Rashomon」(※1), also gives off an unforgettable appeal. At first glance, the abundance of classical words makes it seem dry and stiff, but when you try reading it aloud, it sounds smooth and flows easily. It is by no means expressing complicated, elaborate ideas. By completely eliminating everything superfluous and using only carefully sharpened, minimalist wording, the author vividly brings the setting to life. Once again, I deeply felt that literature is not beautiful because it is decorated with glitter and brilliance; rather, it is beautiful precisely because it lacks embellishment and ostentation.

（※1）Rashomon: the title of a novel.

（※2）Issai no: all, entire.

（※3）Togisumasareta: carefully polished, with nothing unnecessary.

Thanks to the active efforts of explorers such as Columbus, Magellan, and Captain Cook, geographical discoveries, including those in the South Pacific, had essentially come to an end by the seventeenth century. Although it could not be said that the overall appearance of the Earth was complete, it had become more or less clear. Humanity was then faced with a major question.

How was the Earth created? Why are so many species of plants and animals living on Earth? Once geographical discoveries had temporarily settled down, the interest of explorers and adventurers gradually shifted toward discovering plant and animal species that had never been seen before.

Is miso soup really the only reason that person lived so long? Perhaps the person was simply born into a family with genes associated with longevity. Or perhaps they were fortunate enough to survive without contracting infectious diseases such as tuberculosis during a time when medical care was not as advanced as it is today. Of course, asking about the secret to longevity may be worthwhile, but is it not overly simplistic to think that doing exactly the same thing will allow you to live a long life too?

（※1）Longevity: Living for a long time

（※2）Secret: A particularly effective method unknown to others

Dear Mr. Tsuyoshi Nakamura,

Thank you very much for ordering five「A20 Children's Aprons」on March 30.

However, this product is currently out of stock, and we sincerely apologize, but we are unable to accept your order at this time. We urgently contacted the manufacturer to confirm the situation, but unfortunately the manufacturer is also out of stock, so we cannot prepare the quantity you ordered.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Enzo Co., Ltd.—Sales Department
Masaru Takagi
takagi@enzo.co.jp
