The predatory behavior of deep-sea fish reveals unique methods adapted to their habitat. This is because they live under harsh conditions, such as darkness, low water temperatures, and scarce food.

Making part of the body glow to search for prey or lure it closer is one representative method. Another is to ambush prey instead of actively swimming around in search of food. By reducing their muscle mass and avoiding unnecessary movement, they do not expend too much energy, which gives them an advantage for survival. Furthermore, by remaining still and avoiding detection, they greatly reduce the risk of encountering natural enemies that are roaming around hunting.

（※1）おびきよせたりする (to lure closer): to trick the other party into coming near.

（※2）待ち伏せ (ambush): hiding and waiting for the other party to come.

（※3）天敵 (natural enemy): another living creature that specifically preys on that creature.
default.q.test-34-q7-7.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) 作品に触れた人の気持ちを理解すること
The author is no longer satisfied with merely looking at the outside of a work, but longs to deeply understand the thoughts and feelings of the people connected with it, from its creators to those who used it at the time.
default.q.test-34-q7-7.explanation: The key to the answer is the opening sentence of paragraph 3:「何度も博物館に通ううちに、私は、展示品をただ鑑賞するだけではもの足りなくなってきた。」 The complete translation is: “As I visited the museum repeatedly, I began to feel that merely looking at the exhibits was not enough.” The grammar pattern「V-る/V-ている＋うちに」describes a natural change that occurs while an action is repeated. Combined with「もの足りない」(incomplete or unsatisfying) and the change-of-state pattern「〜てくる」(to gradually become...), it directly paraphrases「満足できなくなった」(could no longer feel satisfied). The author then explains what they truly wanted to understand:「①このようなことがわからないと、その時代にこの絵皿を使用していた人の気持ちまでは想像できないのだ。」(“If we do not understand such things, we cannot even imagine the feelings of the people who used this decorated plate in that era.”) The phrase「作品に触れた人」(people who came into contact with the work) in (b) broadly includes both the「作り手」(maker), who expressed feelings through the snow design, and the「使用していた人」(person who used the plate directly in its historical context). Do not confuse this with (a): the author already found it easy to imagine how the object was used, as shown by「細かいことも想像しやすい」. Also reject (c), because researching was only the subsequent action taken to resolve the author’s uncertainty, not what they were dissatisfied with.
default.q.test-34-q7-7.why.0: ✗ (a) Imagining how an object is used is something the author already found easy to do in paragraph 2; it is not what the author felt dissatisfied with.
default.q.test-34-q7-7.why.1: ✓ (b) Paragraph 3 clearly states that the author is no longer satisfied with merely looking at the work, but wants to understand the thoughts and feelings of the person who made it and the people who use it.
default.q.test-34-q7-7.why.2: ✗ (c) Looking up information in an explanatory book or going to the library was the author’s subsequent solution, not something the author felt dissatisfied with.
default.q.test-34-q7-7.why.3: ✗ (d) The passage contains no information at all about the author considering points for improving the work.
default.q.test-8-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) 若い人と同じ時代に生きていないように感じるから。
Older people are shocked because not understanding young people’s language makes them keenly aware of the generation gap and feel that they are no longer living in the same era as younger people.
default.q.test-8-q1-1.explanation: Grammatically, the author uses the particle 「〜こそ」 after a noun or nominalized clause, as in ことばが通じること + こそ, to give strong emphasis meaning “precisely” or “indeed.” It is common in formal argumentative writing to highlight the key factor, and it appears with the explanatory cause pattern 「なぜなら〜からだ」 (“the reason is that …”). The direct evidence is the final sentence of the excerpt: 「なぜなら、ことばが通じることこそ、現代という共通の時代を生きている同時代人のあかしだからです。」 This means: “Because the fact that people can understand one another’s language is precisely proof that they are contemporaries living in the same modern era.” When new language appears and disrupts communication, older people become afraid because they feel separated from the era in which the younger generation lives. A common trap is choosing (a) or (d) based on surface words such as 「恐怖」 (fear) or 「流行」 (trend). For N2 reading comprehension, follow the causal connector 「なぜなら」 and recognize the paraphrase between 「同時代人」 (contemporaries) in the passage and 「若い人と同じ時代に生きていない」 in the correct answer.
default.q.test-8-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The passage does not say that older people feel anxious simply because they hear words they do not understand; their fear comes from the gap between generations.
default.q.test-8-q1-1.why.1: ✓ (b) This is correct because the author states that understanding the language is evidence of belonging to the same era. When the words no longer make sense, people feel as if they no longer live in the same age as younger people.
default.q.test-8-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) The passage only states that older people perceive a generation gap; it does not mention the idea that it would be better if there were no gap.
default.q.test-8-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) What frightens them is the feeling of being out of step with the times because they can no longer understand the language, not fear caused by not knowing the latest trends.
default.q.test-9-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) エネルギーが節約でき、他の魚に食べられる可能性も低くなるから。
Ambush tactics help deep-sea fish avoid excessive energy expenditure in an environment with little food, while also greatly reducing the risk of being detected and attacked by predators.
default.q.test-9-q1-1.explanation: The question uses the N2 grammar pattern 「〜のではなく」(the plain form of a verb + のではなく), meaning “not A, but B,” to reject the usual option and emphasize the action chosen in the second clause. The complete translation is: “Why do they choose to lie in ambush instead of actively swimming around in search of prey?” The reason is identified in the two sentences connected by 「そのうえ」: 「それは筋肉の量を減らし、必要以上に動かないでいれば、体力を使いすぎず、生存に有利になるからだ。そのうえ、目立たないようにじっとしていれば、えさを追い求めて動き回る天敵に会う危険もかなり減るのだ。」 (That is because reducing the amount of muscle and not moving more than necessary prevents excessive energy expenditure and benefits survival. Moreover, staying still so as not to attract attention considerably reduces the risk of encountering predators moving around in search of prey.) These two points are fully paraphrased in choice (d): not using much physical strength means saving energy, while avoiding predators means reducing the risk of being eaten. Do not choose the trap choice (c) merely because it contains the keyword 「筋肉」. The passage presents muscle reduction as a structural feature that reduces energy consumption; it does not say that they “cannot swim for long,” which would distort the causal relationship.
default.q.test-9-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The passage does not mention at all that swimming too much would cause the prey to notice them.
default.q.test-9-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) The claim that the eyes cannot see clearly in the darkness of the deep sea is a personal inference and is not stated in the passage.
default.q.test-9-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) The error is that the passage says the muscle mass was reduced to limit energy expenditure; it does not say that weak muscles made it impossible to swim for a long time.
default.q.test-9-q1-1.why.3: ✓ (d) This correctly reflects both reasons given in the passage: using less energy and avoiding encounters with natural enemies, thereby reducing the risk of being eaten.
